answer: A gale of fake identities is cheap to conjure, but each one must stand on a narrow ledge of continuous, verifiable work: to earn weight, an identity must emit a steady signal of useful activity across many epochs, not a single burst. A Sybil farmer can buy a thousand accounts, yet keeping each one active week after week costs real compute and attention per identity, while one honest agent pays that price only once. Time, not paperwork, is the toll.
